terms.meaning: an international standard of three-letter country codes, such as GBR for the United Kingdom
a fixed list that finds a value from a key, here from a country name to a code

sections.name: ISO3
sections.title: Country code lookup table
sections.what: A fixed list that maps common country names, in lowercase, to three-letter codes such as USA or GBR, with a few short forms such as uk and drc also accepted. The collation rings use these codes as labels.
sections.why: The header says codes follow the ISO standard where known, and that other names get a readable short form. The reason for the table itself is only partly stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Lookups need the exact spelling in lowercase, so a country written another way will miss the table and get a generated code.

sections.name: cleanCountry
sections.title: Tidying a raw country name
sections.what: Takes the country text from a yard record, removes any bracketed region such as a province, and keeps only the first country if several are listed. It returns Country not recorded when nothing usable remains, and the result is the country name shown on the collation view.
sections.why: Likely reason: yard records often add a region or a second country, and the rings must group each project under one plain name. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Only the first country in a list is kept, so a project listing several countries is grouped under the first one alone.

sections.name: countryCode
sections.title: Turning a country name into a code
sections.what: Gives a short code for a country name. It first checks the table. If the name is not there, it returns N/A for unknown or unrecorded countries, and otherwise builds a code from the initials of multi-word names, or from the first three letters, capped at four characters.
sections.why: The header says a readable short form is used for names not in the table. The reason beyond that is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Generated codes can look like real ISO codes without being official, so a reader may take a short form as the standard code.

summary: Turns messy country names from yard records into one clean country name and a short code for the collation rings.
purpose: Keeps the country labels on the collation view consistent from one project to the next.
why: The header says yard country text often has a region in brackets, and that codes follow the ISO standard where known. The reason for the other rules is not stated in the code.
how: A fixed lookup table maps common lowercase country names to three-letter codes. Cleaning removes bracketed text and keeps only the first listed country, or returns Country not recorded if nothing is left. The code function looks up the lowercase name, handles unknown values, and otherwise builds a short code from initials or first letters.
inputs: Raw country text, which may be empty, contain brackets, or list several countries.
outputs: A clean country name, or Country not recorded. A short code such as USA, or N/A for unknown countries.
risks: Countries missing from the table get a generated code that can look like an official code but is not. Only the first country in a list is kept.
debug: If a ring shows a strange code, check whether the country name is in the table with its exact lowercase spelling. If a project lands in the wrong ring, check the raw country text for separators such as semicolons or slashes.
